answer: Every bid must carry a proof-of-work receipt, like a sable pelt at the gate. First, the registry hands the bidder a puzzle bound to the job's hash, so answers can't be reused. Second, the agent burns sixty seconds of CPU, about five cents, and attaches the receipt. Third, any peer verifies it in a millisecond; a bid without one is dropped. A thousand-clone farm placing ten bids each per epoch spends $500 an epoch, $12,000 a month, while one honest agent pays fifty cents. Like a reef, each grain of compute is cheap alone, but together they build a crystal-clear wall no swarm can cross.
